grammar.title: 二 vs 两 for the number two
grammar.pattern: 两 + measure word / 二 in counting and labels
grammar.explanation: Both 二 (èr) and 两 (liǎng) mean "two", but they aren't interchangeable. Use 两 before a measure word like 个 when counting things (两个), and use 二 for counting in sequence, dates, and labels like 二月 (February) or 第二 (second).

grammar.title: 杯 as a measure word for drinks
grammar.explanation: 杯 (bēi) is the measure word for cups or glasses of a drink: 一杯水 ("a cup of water"). Like 个, it goes between the number and the noun and is required — you can't say 一水.

sentences.en: I'd like a cup of water.
How many cups do you want?

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ yī kàn jiù míngbai le.
sentences.en: As soon as I saw it, I understood.
